segments.say: Room temperature is 293 Kelvin, while deep space sits at 2.7.
NASA's Cold Atom Lab chills atoms to under 100 picokelvin, a billion times colder than space.
The Boomerang Nebula is 5,000 light-years away, but NASA's freezer is 250 miles up.

held_for: judge: Generic starfield tiles and flat teal shapes stand in for the data. The two huge contrasts (293 K vs 2.7 K vs picokelvin, and 5,000 light-years vs 250 miles) are never actually shown, and the labels are cut off or meaningless.

judge.one_line: Generic starfield tiles and flat teal shapes stand in for the data. The two huge contrasts (293 K vs 2.7 K vs picokelvin, and 5,000 light-years vs 250 miles) are never actually shown, and the labels are cut off or meaningless.
problems: Hook: the opening frames are a static grid of identical purple tiles under 'Room temperature 293'. Nothing in them says 'coldest place in the universe is above your head'.
seg0/seg1: the tile grid ('each = 20') never changes when the narration moves from 293 K to 2.7 K, and starfield tiles are the wrong icon for temperature.
seg2: 'a billion times colder' is drawn as a circle labelled '1' next to '0.0'. The defining number becomes zero and the claim is lost.
seg3: a flat teal square showing '29400T' for about 6s. The unit is unreadable, nothing moves, and it is a bare number card.
seg4: '29,399,999,999,999,752 apa' is cut off at the right edge, 'NASA's Cold ...' is truncated, and the ending gives no 'whoa'.
Data never causes anything: he holds a stamp, perches on shapes and poses on a ladder.
fixes: Hook: open on Data in a lab coat looking up at the ISS freezer 250 miles overhead, with a frost burst or thermometer plunging past 'deep space' at frame 1.
seg0/seg1: draw a thermometer Data pumps down from 293 K to 2.7 K, with the mercury actually falling, on a temperature-specific visual instead of starfield tiles.
seg2: use a log-scale ladder or descending staircase from 2.7 K down to 100 picokelvin, nine orders of magnitude, with Data climbing down each 'x10' step so 'a billion' becomes distance travelled.
seg3: replace the area square with a log-scale distance tape: 250 miles to the ISS vs 5,000 light-years to the Boomerang Nebula, in readable units, with Data reeling out the tape.
Fit-check every label inside the frame and never format light-years as a T-suffixed or 20-digit raw number.
Update the header label when the beat changes so the on-screen values match what is said.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
